title: Windows: `/etc/environment` is not loaded anymore since 6.2.0
body:
### Issue Description I am not sure if it's an issue - most probably due to the switch to `systemd = true` on windows - the `/etc/environment` is no longer loaded when running `wsl -d podman-machine-default`. It's not an issue for me but a change. On our side we put the proxy-env into * `/etc/systemd/system.conf.d/<>.conf` to have the proxy settings in place when using `podman.exe`
as far as I can say these settings also apply for `podman.exe machine ssh` * `/etc/environment` to get `podman`/`curl`/.. working when troubleshooting something in `podman-machine-default` (e.g. invoked using `wsl -d podman-machine-default`) . Without `/etc/environment` proxy environment loading - users cannot use podman when they invoke `wsl -d podman-machine-default`. I know the 'official' way of WSL would be to put the variables into `.bashrc` . The Proxy-Forwarding feature of WSL doesn't work reliable enough. I put our trick using `/etc/profile.d` below. ### Steps to reproduce the issue Steps to reproduce the issue 1. podman machine init 2. wsl -d podman-machine-default 3. export ### Describe the results you received - ### Describe the results you expected Describe the results you expected- ### podman info output ```yaml 6.2.0 ``` ### Podman in a container No ### Privileged Or Rootless None ### Upstream Latest Release Yes ### Additional environment details _No response_ ### Additional information I managed to re-mimic the `/etc/environment` behavior using a `/etc/profile.d/02-load-etc-environment` inset ```bash if [ ! -e "/proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/WSLInterop" ] && [ ! -e "/run/WSL" ]; then return fi export $(grep -v -e '^#' -e '^PATH=' /etc/environment | xargs -d '\n') ``` Another side-note. When the proxy related variables are in `/etc/environment` these are automatically persistent when using `sudo` as no `pam` is in place.

comments.body:
In general, `wsl -d` is something we don't support, and I would discourage using it. The rationale is that users shouldn't even know there is a VM. If users feel the need to open a shell in the VM, it means that we are doing something wrong. So please tell us why sometimes you need to open a shell in the VM and we will try to fix that.

Anyway, something looks weird because podman remote client forwards the proxy variables:
- At machine init using [WSLENV](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/filesystems#share-environment-variables-between-windows-and-wsl-with-wslenv) for every `wsl -d` commands it executes to setup the distribution.
- At machine start we use [this script](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/9c633d3eb4d38769f97a8dc4284332c7d94b8995/pkg/machine/proxyenv/env.go#L16) to forward the proxy environment variables to:
  - `/etc/systemd/system.conf.d/default-env.conf` (podman rootful service conf)
  - `/etc/systemd/user.conf.d/default-env.conf` (podman rootless service conf)
  - `/etc/environment.d/default-env.conf` (systemd user sessions)
  - `/etc/profile.d/default-env.sh` (user login sessions)

So, if the machine was started with `podman machine start`, then with `wsl -d` the environment variables should be set through `/etc/profile.d/default-env.sh`. I need to test it, though, but I don't think we need to set `/etc/environment`.

@l0rd lets start with the easy things

> So please tell us why sometimes you need to open a shell in the VM and we will try to fix that.
Quite simple - as I try to report problems to you ;-) . It's about history. We started using podman in the early 4.x timeframe. Back then `wsl` had no proxy forwarding feature (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/wsl-config#wslconfig look for `autoProxy`), also podman did not have a proxy environment forwarding, also `WSLENV` did not exist.

What might be more interesting is that our IT decided not to set the `{http,https,no}_proxy` (and the uppercase variants) on Windows hosts. Our experience values are that multiple programs show misbehavior when those are set. For that reason we set the proxy environment variables manually for each WSL1/2 environment (recently learned those are not VMs but namespaces).

How do we setup podman? We are using a playbook passed with `podman machine init` to adapt the `podman-machine-default` to our internal requirements e.g. certificate chain (for versions where `--import-native-ca` is not available), local dockerproxy, and also corporate proxy (using `/etc/systemd/`). My experience shows that it's useful to have the `podman-machine-default` functional on it's own - for as I said troubleshooting.

> `/etc/profile.d/default-env.sh` (user login sessions)
That thing is new to me (must have missed that over time). Nice feature.

> side note to `autoProxy` in `.wslconfig`
As far as I understood this feature takes the Window Network connection proxy settings and (tries) to forward them to WSL.
Why _tries_
* we are using a .pac file
* in the wsl 2.x version frame it only set `http_proxy` 
* since wsl 3.x version frame it only set `http_proxy` `https_proxy`
* but `no_proxy` was never handled correctly on our side by wsl directly

As I initially said - not a problem - but a difference.

If I would be allowed to post feature requests:
* add a config file for podman.exe aka podman-remote that can be used to set the environment for the `podman-machine-default`
* hide `podman-machine-default` from Windows Terminal (e.g. via `/etc/wsl-distribution.conf`)
* add a prompt to interactive login shells from `wsl -d podman-machine-default` that state that using this mode is not recommended/intended
* as you said `The rationale is that users shouldn't even know there is a VM.`
* afaik it's not possible to prevent that `podman-machine-default` becomes default when it's the first VM

feel free to close the ticket

> 1. add a config file for podman.exe aka podman-remote that can be used to set the environment for the podman-machine-default
> 2. hide podman-machine-default from Windows Terminal (e.g. via /etc/wsl-distribution.conf)
> 3. add a prompt to interactive login shells from wsl -d podman-machine-default that state that using this mode is not recommended/intended
> 4. as you said The rationale is that users shouldn't even know there is a VM.
> 5. afaik it's not possible to prevent that podman-machine-default becomes default when it's the first VM

Thank you @userid0x0, that's a good list. I will keep that in mind. We want to avoid breaking current users' environments, so 2) and 5) are probably for Podman v7. But we should be able to implement 1) and 3) in Podman v6.

I am not closing this issue because I have found a problem with `/etc/profile.d/default-env.sh` (that predates the systemd enablement) and I am fixing it.
